findings.claim: The specification groups processes into categories: material removal (cutting, filing, drilling), shaping and manipulation (turning, milling, forming), and preparation and finishing.
findings.truth: The specification identifies material removal, shaping and manipulation, joining and assembly, and heat and chemical treatment as applications of engineering processes.

findings.claim: A joining process that uses a brass or copper-based filler alloy with a melting point above 450°C; the parent metals do not melt.
findings.truth: Brazing uses a filler metal above 450°C but below the melting temperature of the parent metals. Filler alloys are not limited to brass or copper-based alloys.
findings.evidence: TWI What is Brazing? FAQ; Wikipedia Brazing (filler materials)

findings.claim: Clamp the workpiece in a machine vice secured to the drill table — eliminates the snagging/spinning hazard.
findings.truth: Clamping controls the risk of the workpiece spinning if the drill bit snags; it does not eliminate the hazard.
findings.evidence: HSE Managing risks and risk assessment at work: Overview

findings.claim: Tie back long hair; tuck in loose clothing and remove jewellery — eliminates entanglement risk.
findings.truth: These actions reduce entanglement risk; they are control measures, not elimination of the hazard.
findings.evidence: HSE Managing risks and risk assessment at work: Overview
